headline: BIS renews for one year the temporary denial order against URAL Airlines JSC (Russia)
what_changed: BIS granted OEE's request to renew the temporary denial order (TDO) issued in this matter on September 30, 2025 against URAL Airlines JSC [FR Doc. 2026-19927, preamble]. OEE submitted the written renewal request on August 13, 2026 [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section I]. The renewal runs for one year [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV]. Section II.A states that in cases demonstrating a pattern of repeated, ongoing and/or continuous apparent violations, BIS may request renewal for an additional period not exceeding one year [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section II.A]. Footnote 3 in Section I states that, at the time of the earlier renewal, Section 766.24(d) provided for additional 180-day renewal periods [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section I, n.3]. The Assistant Secretary found that Ural violated the Regulations and the TDO, that the violations were significant and deliberate, and that there is a likelihood of imminent violations [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section III]. The extended period rests on a finding that Ural engaged in a pattern of repeated, ongoing and/or continuous apparent violations of the EAR [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section III]. BIS's evidence lists flights dated June 25, 2026 to August 26, 2026 by three aircraft (serial numbers 05055, 02343 and 07206; types A320-232 and A321-231) into and out of Russia from/to Sukhumi, Dushanbe, Khujand and Kulob, and domestically within Russia [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section II.B, table]. The table includes flight dates of August 17, 2026 and August 26, 2026, which are later than the August 13, 2026 request date, and the source does not explain this [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section II.B, table]. The order is dated September 24, 2026 and is effective immediately [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV].
who_is_affected: The respondent is URAL Airlines JSC, Utrenniy Lane 1-g, Yekaterinburg, Russia 620025 [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV, First]. The first paragraph of the order also covers Ural's successors, assigns, agents and employees when acting for or on its behalf [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV, First]. Under the second paragraph, no person may, directly or indirectly, export, reexport or transfer (in-country) to or on behalf of Ural any item subject to the EAR, except as directly related to safety of flight and authorized by BIS [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV, Second A]. Any other person related to Ural by ownership, control, position of responsibility, affiliation or other connection in the conduct of trade or business may be made subject to the order after notice and opportunity for comment under section 766.23 [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV, Third].
instruments: Order Renewing Temporary Denial of Export Privileges (15 CFR 766.24)
Export Control Reform Act of 2018, 50 U.S.C. 4820(a)(5) (cited as authority for TDOs)

Published in the Federal Register September 29, 2026 [FR Doc. 2026-19927, header]
licence_posture: The order bars Ural from applying for, obtaining or using any license (except directly related to safety of flight), license exception, or export control document [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV, First A]. The other prohibitions in the order carry an exception for activity directly related to safety of flight and authorized by BIS pursuant to Section 764.3(a)(2) of the Regulations [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV, First B-C; Second A-E]. The source states that BIS will review export or reexport license applications for aircraft and parts specified in ECCN 9A991 destined to Russia under a policy of denial [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section II.B]. The source states that aircraft registered in, owned or controlled by, or under charter or lease by Russia or a national of Russia are excluded from license exception AVS [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section II.B]. The source states that a U.S.-origin aircraft, or a foreign aircraft that includes more than 25% controlled U.S.-origin content, that is registered in, owned or controlled by, or under charter or lease by Russia or a national of Russia is subject to a license requirement before it can travel to Russia [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section II.B].
relevance_eu_exporters: The second paragraph of the order applies to 'any person' and covers export, reexport and transfer (in-country) of items subject to the EAR to or on behalf of Ural [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV, Second A]. It also covers servicing of items of whatever origin owned, possessed or controlled by Ural if the service involves the use of an item subject to the EAR that has been or will be exported from the United States [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV, Second E]. The source states that a foreign aircraft including more than 25% controlled U.S.-origin content, and registered in, owned or controlled by, or under charter or lease by Russia or a national of Russia, is subject to a license requirement before it can travel to Russia [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section II.B]. The source states that the renewal is intended to give notice to companies and individuals in the United States and abroad that they should avoid dealing with Ural in connection with export and reexport transactions involving items subject to the Regulations [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section III]. The source does not reference a foreign direct product rule in the order text [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV].

Note that the safety-of-flight exception requires BIS authorization pursuant to Section 764.3(a)(2) [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV, Second].

Note that servicing of Ural-held items is covered where the service involves the use of an item subject to the EAR exported or to be exported from the United States [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV, Second E].

Note that Ural may appeal the order to the Office of the Administrative Law Judge, and that a renewal request may be opposed by written submission received not later than seven days before the expiration date [FR Doc. 2026-19927, Section IV].

headline: BIS renews Azur Air temporary denial order for one year (Russia aviation, ECCN 9A991)
what_changed: BIS granted the Office of Export Enforcement's request to renew the temporary denial order issued on September 16, 2025 against Azur Air [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Preamble]. The renewal runs for one year [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section IV]. OEE submitted its written renewal request on August 3, 2026 [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section I]. The order states that, given the temporary suspension of international mail service to Russia, OEE attempted to deliver the request to Azur by alternative means, and that no opposition to the renewal was received [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section I]. The order records the TDO history as an initial 180-day order signed April 7, 2022, renewed on October 3, 2022, March 29, 2023, September 23, 2023, September 20, 2024 and September 16, 2025 [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section I]. The order states that this renewal reflects a corrected address for Azur, which was introduced by a modification of the September 20, 2024 renewal order dated January 31, 2025 in the text (footnote 5 refers to a January 30, 2025 modification order) [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section I]. The Assistant Secretary found that BIS's evidence convincingly demonstrates that Azur violated the Regulations and the TDO, that the violations were significant and deliberate, and that there is a likelihood of imminent violations [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section III]. The order bases the one-year period on a finding that Azur engaged in a pattern of repeated, ongoing and/or continuous apparent violations of the EAR [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section III]. The order's table lists flights dated March 9, 2026 to July 17, 2026 by Boeing 757 aircraft (tail numbers RA-73071, RA-73029, RA-73076 and RA-73072) between Russia and Turkey, Vietnam or Thailand, and within Russia [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section II.B]. The order is dated September 11, 2026 and is effective immediately [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section IV].
who_is_affected: The named respondent is Azur Air, Office 29, Vzletnaya St. 57, Krasnoyarsk, Russia 660020 [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section IV]. Under the order's first paragraph, Azur, when acting for or on its behalf, and any successors or assigns, agents or employees may not directly or indirectly participate in any transaction involving items subject to the EAR that are exported or to be exported from the United States, or in any other activity subject to the EAR [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section IV, First]. Under the second paragraph, no person may export, reexport or transfer (in-country) any item subject to the EAR to or on behalf of Azur, except as directly related to safety of flight and authorized by BIS under Section 764.3(a)(2) [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section IV, Second.A]. The same paragraph also restricts any person from facilitating Azur's acquisition of, acquiring from Azur, or servicing items subject to the EAR that have been or will be exported from the United States, subject to the same safety-of-flight exception [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section IV, Second.B-E]. Any other person related to Azur by ownership, control, position of responsibility, affiliation or other connection in the conduct of trade or business may be made subject to the order after notice and opportunity for comment under Section 766.23 [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section IV, Third]. The tail numbers and serial numbers listed in the table are RA-73071 (SN 29377), RA-73029 (SN 26330), RA-73076 (SN 30043) and RA-73072 (SN 29382) [FR Doc. 2026-19021, Section II.B].

headline: BIS renews one-year Temporary Denial Order against PJSC Aeroflot for continued EAR violations

headline: Commission adopts 2026 update of EU dual-use control list (Annex I, Reg. 2021/821); not yet in force
what_changed: On 14 September 2026 the European Commission adopted a Delegated Regulation updating the EU dual-use export control list in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 [C(2026)6323]. The announcement states that the update aligns the list with 2025 decisions of the Wassenaar Arrangement, the Australia Group and the Nuclear Suppliers Group, and includes commitments Member States accepted as Wassenaar members to control additional items uniformly [C(2026)6323]. The announcement states that the update adds new dual-use items, including semiconductor manufacturing and testing equipment and materials, advanced computing integrated circuits and electronic assemblies such as ICs incorporating one or multiple Digital Processing Units, ceramic matrix composites reinforced with mullite, inductive-sensing rotary encoders, additive manufacturing equipment for energetic materials, chemical vapour deposition equipment for silicon carbide fibres, and technology for the development of axial compressors of gas turbine engines [C(2026)6323]. The semiconductor examples given are atomic layer deposition equipment for molybdenum and ruthenium, equipment for the development and inspection of Extreme Ultra-Violet masks and reticles, and single wafer cleaning equipment [C(2026)6323]. The announcement also states that certain control parameters are modified and certain technical definitions and descriptions are updated [C(2026)6323]. The act was adopted by the Commission and is not yet published in the Official Journal or in force; it enters into force upon publication in the Official Journal after the usual two-month scrutiny period for the Council and the European Parliament [C(2026)6323].
who_is_affected: The announcement states that the EU control list is a common list of dual-use items that must be controlled in all Member States [C(2026)6323]. It refers to uniform EU-level controls and a level-playing-field for economic operators, without naming specific operators, entry codes or destinations [C(2026)6323].
effective_dates: Adopted by the Commission: 14 September 2026 (adoption date, not an in-force date) [C(2026)6323]
Entry into force: "upon publication in the Official Journal after the usual two-month scrutiny period for the Council and the European Parliament"; no calendar date stated in source [C(2026)6323]
licence_posture: The announcement states no licence requirement, licence exception, presumption or case-by-case policy [C(2026)6323]. It states only that the listed items are added to the EU control list, which must be controlled in all Member States [C(2026)6323].
relevance_eu_exporters: The act amends Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2021/821, the common EU control list, and applies through that list once it enters into force after publication in the Official Journal [C(2026)6323]. The announcement does not state any foreign direct product rule, de minimis, transshipment or remote-access provision [C(2026)6323]. Entry-level text, thresholds and the Comprehensive Change Note Summary are not reproduced in the source provided and are not stated in source [C(2026)6323].

headline: BIS moves firearm sound suppressors from ITAR to EAR, adds new ECCNs and TMP tools-of-trade exception
what_changed: BIS revised the EAR and CCL to control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors that are being removed from the USML by a companion State Department IFR, creating new item paragraphs 0A501.f (suppressors usable with rifles/pistols under 0A501, 0A506, 0A507, or interchangeably with shotguns) and 0A502.f (suppressors for exclusive use with shotguns under 0A502/0A508) [FR Doc. 2026-14942, SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION, Section I.B]. New reasons for control (NS1/RS1/FC1/UN/AT1 for 0A501.f; FC1/UN/AT1 plus a new RS control for 0A502.f) and license exception eligibility (LVS, BAG, STA, TMP) were added for the new paragraphs [FR Doc. 2026-14942, Section I.C-D]. BIS also revised License Exception TMP (Sec. 740.9) to add a new paragraph (a)(2) authorizing temporary export/reexport of firearms and related items, including suppressors, as 'tools of trade' without a license, subject to quantity limits and effective-control/return conditions [FR Doc. 2026-14942, Section II]. Sec. 758.10 entry-clearance requirements for temporary imports were broadened from listed end-item ECCNs to all 0x5zz and certain '600 series' items subject to the EAR that are also on the USMIL [FR Doc. 2026-14942, Section III].
who_is_affected: Exporters, reexporters, and manufacturers of firearm sound suppressors and related firearms parts/components/accessories/attachments classified under ECCNs 0A501, 0A502, 0A506, 0A507, and 0A508; employers whose employees carry company-owned firearms abroad as tools of trade; and temporary importers of firearms-related items that are also listed on the USMIL [FR Doc. 2026-14942, SUMMARY; Sections I-III].
instruments: 15 CFR 740 (License Exceptions, including Sec. 740.9 TMP and Sec. 740.14 BAG)

July 23, 2026 (amendatory instructions 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11, including Sec. 740.9 TMP revision, Sec. 740.14 BAG revision, Sec. 758.1 and 758.10 revisions, and the July 23, 2026 version of ECCN 0A502)
Savings clause deadline: August 24, 2026 for shipments en route as of July 23, 2026 under prior NLR/license exception eligibility
licence_posture: An EAR authorization is required to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) sound suppressors newly added under ECCNs 0A501.f and 0A502.f, including related technology and software, to foreign persons in the US or abroad [FR Doc. 2026-14942, Section I.B]. Applications are generally reviewed case-by-case under the existing RS licensing policy at Sec. 742.6(b)(1)(i) to determine whether the transaction is contrary to US national security or foreign policy interests [FR Doc. 2026-14942, Section I.C, I.E]. New Sec. 742.6(a)(14) imposes a license requirement for 0A502.f exports/reexports to all destinations except NATO member states, Australia, Austria, India, Ireland, Japan, Liechtenstein, New Zealand, South Korea, or Switzerland, reviewed under paragraph (b)(15)/(b)(1)(i) [FR Doc. 2026-14942, Section I.E; amendment 5]. License exceptions LVS ($500 threshold for Canada), BAG, STA, and the newly revised TMP (Sec. 740.9(a)(2), tools-of-trade) are available for the new paragraphs subject to stated conditions and restrictions under Sec. 740.2 [FR Doc. 2026-14942, Section I.D; Section II].
relevance_eu_exporters: The new RS control at Sec. 742.6(a)(14) exempts exports/reexports of ECCN 0A502.f sound suppressors from the license requirement otherwise applicable to non-listed destinations for NATO member states, Australia, Austria, India, Ireland, Japan, Liechtenstein, New Zealand, South Korea, or Switzerland, with NATO membership determined by cross-reference to Sec. 772.1 of the EAR [FR Doc. 2026-14942, Section I.E; amendment 5, Sec. 742.6(a)(14)]. The source does not identify which countries are NATO members, does not discuss EU membership, and does not state that EU member states are covered by this exemption; any link to EU exporters via this NATO carve-out is therefore indirect only. Beyond this, the source does not address other EU-specific mechanisms such as a foreign direct product rule or de minimis threshold for these ECCNs.

headline: Corrigendum deletes the sub-193 nm light-source criterion from Annex I entry 3B501.f.1.a
what_changed: The corrigendum of 9 February 2026 to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/2003 replaces the text of entry 3B501.f.1.a, 'A light source wavelength shorter than 193 nm; or', with 'Not used;' [OJ L 2026/90092, entry 3B501.f.1.a]. 'Not used' is the Annex I placeholder for a deleted provision: the sub-193 nm light-source criterion no longer exists as a route into entry 3B501.f.1, whose remaining sub-points are unchanged [OJ L 2026/90092, entry 3B501.f.1.a].
who_is_affected: Exporters and holders of prior classifications of align-and-expose step-and-repeat or step-and-scan wafer-processing equipment assessed under entry 3B501.f.1 [CELEX 02021R0821-20251115, entry 3B501.f.1].
effective_dates: Correction applies as part of Regulation (EU) 2025/2003, in force since 15 November 2025 — 'the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal' [CELEX 32025R2003, Art. 2]
licence_posture: not stated in source
relevance_eu_exporters: Directly applicable: Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 governs EU exporters' classification obligations, and the corrected criterion gates entry 3B501.f.1 [OJ L 2026/90092, entry 3B501.f.1.a].
action_items: Revalidate any classification that relied on the deleted sub-193 nm light-source criterion of entry 3B501.f.1.a — including lithography equipment previously caught by it.
Record the Annex I version relied upon (02021R0821-20251115) in the classification register.

reclassification_impact: Holders of prior classifications relying on entry 3B501.f.1.a should revalidate against the corrected entry text: the sub-193 nm light-source criterion no longer exists, and equipment caught solely by it falls outside 3B501.f.1.a.
materiality: Editorial de-duplication, assessed as non-substantive: the deleted criterion of entry 3B501.f.1.a is verbatim-identical to entry 3B001.f.1.a, which the corrigendum did not touch [CELEX 02021R0821-20251115, entry 3B001.f.1.a]. Equipment meeting the sub-193 nm light-source parameter remains controlled under entry 3B001.f.1 — no change to what requires authorisation [CELEX 02021R0821-20251115, entry 3B001.f.1].
